question: Where do most left-handed people have their main language areas?
answer: In the left hemisphere, as in almost all right-handers. Handedness shifts the odds only modestly: among 326 healthy adults tested by Knecht and colleagues, right-hemisphere language rose from 4% of strong right-handers to 27% of strong left-handers. About three strong left-handers in four still speak from the hemisphere that runs their weaker hand.
move: A visible trait is a weak guide to the hidden one it seems to mirror.
trap: Mirroring the hand: left hand, so language on the right.
